bug_semantics: Public safe ruint::algorithms::div::reciprocal_mg10 is a 256-entry MG10 reciprocal lookup. Callers must pass d >= 2^63 so that d9 = d >> 55 is in [256, 511] and (d9 - 256) indexes TABLE. The only guard is debug_assert!(d >= (1 << 63)), which is compiled out in release. The live load is unsafe TABLE.get_unchecked((d9.0 - 256) as usize). Passing d = 0 (or any d < 2^63) makes d9 < 256; the unsigned subtraction wraps to a huge usize and get_unchecked reads outside TABLE, which is UB/memory corruption in safe Rust. The function is re-exported as algorithms::div::reciprocal and is callable by downstream crates.
flaw_origin: 86feced81038c3ebb0ed2ef57b2c0fbd9ffcfb43 (2022-10-20) first added pub fn reciprocal_mg10 with the debug_assert and a bounds-checked TABLE[(d9.0 - 256) as usize] load (OOB panics, not UB). Two days later efeee3d169dfd50275a447a1138933a7caffb6c1 (GMP division) commented out that safe index and wrote the get_unchecked load while leaving the function safe and the debug_assert as the only precondition check. That is the first write of the unsound mechanism. It is a single-parent local commit, not a move/revert/squash of an earlier get_unchecked.
